footer.tagline: An independent, open-source fact-checking project for Kenya.

offline.title: You're offline
offline.body: fact_checker_ke couldn't reach the network. The app shell is cached, so pages you've already visited may still work — reconnect to submit a new claim or load fresh checks.

check.aiAssisted: AI-assisted, confidence-weighted assessment — not a verdict

draft.awaitingEditor: Still being assessed. Evidence and sources are shown below; most checks publish automatically once the evidence is weighed, but this one is held for additional review before publishing.

guidance.claimAttributedNote: We assess the claim, not the person — the evidence speaks to what was said; you decide.

notFound.title: Check not found
notFound.body: We couldn't find a check with that id.

caveat.heading: AI-assisted assessment · pilot · not a verdict on any person.
caveat.draftNotice: Draft caveat — pending advocate review, not a finished legal shield
caveat.tierCNotice: Open question, not a verdict: named person has a right of reply.

legal.advocateMarker: ⚠ Pending legal review — not yet resolved

pages.draftBadge: DRAFT — pending advocate review, not legally binding

terms.title: Terms & Conditions
terms.intro: This page describes a starter draft of our Terms & Conditions, written for an eventual Kenyan advocate's review — it is not yet legally binding.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This page describes a starter draft of our Privacy Policy, written for an eventual Kenyan advocate's review — it is not yet legally binding.
privacy.retentionHeading: What we collect, per data class

consent.enableLabel: Yes, use my submissions and signals to help improve and train your models
consent.severabilityNote: Optional and separate from submitting a claim — leaving this off does not stop you from using fact_checker_ke.
consent.statusOn: Saved: you've opted in on this device. You can change this at any time.
consent.statusOff: Saved: you have not opted in. Nothing of yours is used for training.
consent.specialCategoryNote: Protest-related or other special-category content is excluded from training by default, regardless of this choice.

submit.heading: fact_checker_ke
submit.lede: Two ways a claim gets checked: we catch what's trending, or you submit one. Either way, AI weighs the evidence and publishes a confidence-weighted assessment, sources cited — you decide. People audit results afterward and can correct them.

smartInput.placeholder: Paste a link, or type what they said…
smartInput.label: Paste a link or type a claim

detected.text: Free text — we'll check this claim directly

moment.heading: Mark the moment + the claim
moment.help: Drag to the moment they said it, then type or paste exactly what they said — we check that quoted text, we never download or clip the video itself.
moment.noEmbed: We don't have a live preview for this platform yet — the link itself is still submitted and checked.

upload.heading: Or share your own photo or video
upload.help: Drag a file here, click to browse, or paste from your clipboard.
upload.trust: Uploads are scanned and stripped of location/device data on our server before any human reviews them (ADR-0027).
upload.rights: I own this media or have the right to share it, it is not of a minor, and I consent to its use for fact-checking.

nextSteps.heading: What happens next
nextSteps.verifying: AI weighs the evidence and sets a confidence
nextSteps.ready: Published as a confidence-weighted assessment, sources cited — a human audits it afterward

submit.awaitingReview: Awaiting assessment — not a verdict yet
submit.success: Submitted. Watch it move through the pipeline.

error.offline: You're offline — submitting a new claim needs a connection.
error.empty: Paste a link or type a claim before submitting.

status.heading: Tracking your submission

desc.received: Your submission is queued for analysis.
desc.analyzing: Extracting claims and translating, keeping the original words.
desc.analyzed: Claims extracted. Matching each one against credible sources.
desc.verifying: Weighing the evidence and setting a confidence level for the assessment.
desc.failed: Something went wrong processing this submission.

status.readyHeld: Assessed and held for editor review before publishing — not yet public.
status.polling: Live updates unavailable — checking periodically instead.

tracker.heading: Maandamano advisories
tracker.intro: Read-only advisories by ward and sub-county. No precise locations are published.
tracker.streetHeading: When the streets move, the rumours move faster.
tracker.streetBody: During maandamano, fact_checker_ke tracks confirmed advisories at the ward level — road closures, safety notices, and the claims going viral about them. We show what's happening and where, never who is where.
tracker.streetNote: Protester safety comes before engagement. Locations stay coarse, and anything that could put people at risk is held or dropped.

frozen.title: Tracker temporarily frozen
frozen.body: Advisories are paused while we confirm current conditions. This is a deliberate safety measure, not an outage — check back shortly.

offline.title: Can't confirm current status
offline.body: We never show a cached advisory as current. Reconnect to see the latest status.

empty.title: No active demonstrations tracked right now
empty.body: There are no confirmed maandamano advisories at the moment. When verified advisories come in, they'll appear here by ward and sub-county.

tracker.staleWarning: Not re-verified in over 2 hours — status may be out of date.

media.heading: Clips of this advisory
media.checking: Checking this clip for recycled footage…
media.flaggedBadge: ⚠ May be recycled footage — an earlier copy was seen before this date.

archive.heading: Concluded advisories
archive.intro: Advisories that have ended or been cancelled, with their status history and source links. No live media is served here.

empty.title: No concluded advisories yet
empty.body: When an advisory ends or is cancelled, it will be archived here with its full status history.

feed.heading: What we're checking now
feed.intro: A live stream of recently published assessments — claims we caught trending, and claims readers submitted. Each carries a confidence weight and cited sources; none is a verdict on a person.

viral.heading: Most viral right now
viral.intro: The published claims spreading fastest on the platforms we monitor — ranked by reach, not by rating.

empty.heading: The feed fills as we publish — nothing yet
empty.body: We haven't published an assessment yet. This is an honest empty state, not placeholder data — check back shortly, or submit a claim yourself.

feed.mockNotice: Demo data — the live feed isn't reachable right now, so these are example assessments, not real published checks.
feed.disclosureIntro: The disclosure below applies to every assessment above.

editorial.heading: Editor review

signInRequired.title: Sign-in required
signInRequired.body: The editor workspace is an internal, authenticated-only surface. There is no public editor access, and real editor sign-in is not available yet.

editorial.noRatingToSubmitter: Rating withheld from the submitter until published (AT-0004-B).

scale.ariaLabel: The six-verdict rating scale and what each verdict means

true.name: True
true.description: Backed by credible evidence, with no material caveat.

mostly.name: Mostly true
mostly.description: Accurate in the main — but missing context shifts the picture.

misleading.name: Misleading
misleading.description: Sourced, yet framed to imply what the evidence doesn't.

false.name: False
false.description: Contradicted by the credible evidence we can find.

unproven.name: Unproven
unproven.description: No reliable evidence either way — not yet.

notcheckable.name: Not checkable
notcheckable.description: An opinion, a prediction, or a matter of belief — not a fact.

flow.ariaLabel: How a claim gets checked, from entry to published audit
flow.entriesLabel: How a claim enters — two engines
flow.stepsLabel: What happens once a claim is in

fetch.title: We fetch
fetch.body: We continuously surface viral, trending claims from YouTube, X, and fact-check feeds like PesaCheck and Africa Check — a pilot; TikTok is embed-only, not autonomously monitored.

submit.title: You submit
submit.body: Anyone can submit a link or a quote. The same pipeline checks it next.

extract.title: Extract
extract.body: We pull out the checkable claims and translate them, keeping the original words.

ground.title: Ground
ground.body: Each claim is matched against credible sources — KNBS, Kenya Law, the Hansard, newsrooms.

assess.title: Assess
assess.body: AI weighs the evidence into a confidence-weighted, claim-attributed assessment. We rate claims, not people.

publish.title: Publish
publish.body: It goes live with its sources, a confidence weight, and the standing caveat.

audit.title: Audit
audit.body: A person audits a shrinking sample afterwards, and can correct it.

hero.lede: fact_checker_ke checks claims we spot trending and claims you submit — in English, Swahili, and Sheng. AI weighs each one against the evidence and cites every source; a shrinking sample is audited by a person after publishing. We rate claims, not people.

sample.claim: “Unemployment in Kenya fell to 2% last year.”
sample.rationale: KNBS puts the 2024 unemployment rate near 5.6%. The 2% figure counts only the strictest definition and drops discouraged workers who have stopped looking.
sample.caveat: We rate claims, not people — this is an AI assessment, for research purposes; you decide.

scale.heading: Six verdicts. No opinions.
scale.body: Every claim lands on one of six ratings, each tied to what the evidence actually supports — never to who said it.

pipeline.heading: Two engines, one pipeline
pipeline.body: Most claims we check, we go looking for — the rest, you bring to us. Either way, the same pipeline checks it.

street.heading: When the streets move, the rumours move faster.
street.body: During maandamano, fact_checker_ke tracks confirmed advisories at the ward level — road closures, safety notices, and the claims going viral about them. We show what's happening and where, never who is where.
street.note: Protester safety comes before engagement. Locations stay coarse, and anything that could put people at risk is held or dropped.

independent.title: Independent and open-source.
independent.body: The code is public, and the funding will be too.

cite.title: We cite everything.
cite.body: No verdict ships without the sources it rests on.

audit.title: People audit the AI.
audit.body: A shrinking sample of published assessments is reviewed and corrected after the fact — not gated before every claim goes out.

reply.title: Right of reply.
reply.body: Named people get a correction path and a chance to respond; a claim-level flag is never read as an indictment of a person.

premium.heading: Premium: back the work, lose the ads.
premium.body: A paid tier for readers, researchers, and newsrooms who want more than the free feed — never a tier that changes what gets checked or how. The rating on every claim stays the same whether you pay or not.

adFree.title: No ads, anywhere
adFree.body: A completely ad-free reading experience across every check, every page.

alerts.title: Real-time alerts
alerts.body: Priority, real-time notifications the moment a claim you follow gets a published verdict.

api.title: API & data access
api.body: Pull verdicts, sources, and confidence scores programmatically — built for newsrooms and researchers.

earlyAccess.title: Early access
earlyAccess.body: New verticals, languages, and features before they reach the free tier.

premium.note: No payment today — this just tells us you're interested.

sponsor.heading: Back independent fact-checking.
sponsor.body: Newsrooms, funders, and civic-tech partners can back fact_checker_ke to keep it independent and open — the same way the code already is.
sponsor.firewall: Editorial firewall: sponsors fund the work, not the outcome. No sponsor sees a verdict before the public does, and none gets a vote on it. Every sponsor and grant is listed on our funding-transparency page.

waitlist.heading: Be there when it launches.
waitlist.body: We're building in the open. Leave your email and we'll tell you the day it goes live — no other mail.

contact.title: Contact
contact.intro: Press enquiries, corrections, right-of-reply requests, partnership or contribution questions — reach the founder directly.

card.sourceNote: Details sourced directly from developer.ericgitangu.com; nothing here is invented.

rightOfReply.heading: Right of reply & corrections
rightOfReply.body: If a published check names you and you believe it is wrong, unfair, or missing context, say so here. Every assessment on fact_checker_ke carries a right of reply and correction path — see the Methodology page and the standing caveat on each check.

join.title: How to join the movement
join.intro: fact_checker_ke is a small, open team trying to make Kenya's loudest claims checkable — against evidence, not vibes. It stays useful only if more people help build, check, and spread it.

mission.heading: Why this exists
mission.body: Claims travel faster than corrections, especially in Kenyan WhatsApp groups and timelines during an election, a protest, or a crisis. fact_checker_ke pairs an automated fetch-and-assess engine with a submission flow and async editorial audit, cites every source, shows its confidence, and gives named people a right of reply — see the Methodology page for the full pipeline.

contribute.title: Contribute code or review
contribute.body: The whole stack is open-source on GitHub — pipeline, web app, infra, docs. Issues are labelled for first-time contributors; ADRs explain the reasoning behind the harder calls.

check.title: Submit or flag a claim
check.body: Spot a claim worth checking, or evidence we got wrong? Submitting is the fastest way to help right now — no sign-up required.

partner.title: Partner, sponsor, or go Premium early
partner.body: Newsrooms, civic-tech groups, and funders who want to back independent fact-checking in Kenya can register interest — sponsorship funds the work, never the verdict.

futureNote.heading: Open today — honestly, that may change
futureNote.body: fact_checker_ke is fully open-source and free to use right now. As monetization matures (Premium tiers, sponsorships — see the landing page), parts of the project may move to a gated or private-access model where new contributors request access rather than fork freely. If you want in, the earliest path is registering interest below or opening a pull request today, while everything is still open.

register.heading: Register your interest
register.body: Leave your email and tell us what best describes you — we'll reach out as contributor and partner access opens up.

consent.title: Your privacy choice
consent.body: We'd like to show ads to help fund independent fact-checking. With your consent we'll load them; decline and you'll see none. This never affects which claims we check or how we rate them.

upsell.inlineTitle: Back the work, lose the ads
upsell.inlineBody: Premium is a fully ad-free read — and it funds independent fact-checking without changing a single verdict.
